findings.current: “About 3.7 billion won. Thirty billion of that will be spent on buying the new house.”
findings.defect: The second amount is inflated tenfold: 30억 won is three billion won, not thirty billion.
findings.rationale: The source gives a balance of approximately 3.7 billion won and says three billion won of it will be spent on the house.
findings.replacement: “About 3.7 billion won. Three billion of that will go toward buying the new house.”
findings.source: “약 37억 정도 됩니다. 이 중에 30억 원은 새로운 집 매입 비용으로 나갈 거고요.”

findings.current: “Wouldn’t you? He lived as an F-rank Hunter, then reawakened and suddenly started getting huge sums of money handed to him. Of course he’d be feeling pretty damn good about himself.”
findings.defect: The draft weakens the established reawakening terminology and renders 가오가 확 살다 as merely feeling good rather than his swagger or ego swelling.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly names reawakening and characterizes the sudden money as boosting his swagger, which motivates the observers’ dismissive interpretation of his behavior.
findings.replacement: “Can you blame him? He lived as an F-rank Hunter, then after his reawakening, big chunks of money started rolling in. Of course his ego would swell.”
findings.source: “오죽하겠습니까. F급으로 살다가 재각성 후 목돈 턱턱 들어오니까 가오가 확 살겠죠.”

findings.current: —I have a few places, but… as you know, this neighborhood overlaps with a safety zone, so it’s a little expensive.
findings.defect: Although “overlaps” is close, it is awkward and leaves the geographic relationship unclear; the source says the neighborhood straddles the safety-zone boundary.
findings.rationale: 걸쳐져 있다 describes extending across or straddling an area, not simply being wholly inside it.
findings.replacement: —I do have a few, but… as you know, this neighborhood straddles a safety zone, so it’s a little expensive.
findings.source: - 몇 개 있긴 한데…… 알다시피 이 동네가 안전 구역에 걸쳐져 있어서 좀 비싸.

findings.current:
“Oh my, you’re a Hunter? I knew you looked fit. What rank are you? Ah, is it rude of me to ask something like that?”

—Somewhere around there. It’s not very high. C-rank.

“Oh my, oh my. You must make good money. Can I feel that arm? Oh-ho-ho!”
findings.defect: Two lines in the intercepted conversation incorrectly switch from the established em-dash presentation to ordinary quotation marks.
findings.rationale: All three source lines belong to the same transmitted conversation and should retain the same dialogue formatting as the surrounding intercepted speech.
findings.replacement:
—Oh my, you’re a Hunter? I knew you looked fit. What rank are you? Ah, is it rude of me to ask something like that?

—Somewhere around there. It’s not very high. C-rank.

—Oh my, oh my. You must make good money. Can I feel that arm? Oh-ho-ho!

findings.current: —I thought he might be a gangster, so I couldn’t say a word.
findings.defect: The draft omits the comic and emphatic force of 찍소리 못 했다, which means she could not so much as squeak.
findings.rationale: 찍소리 preserves both her intimidation and the deliberately vivid, colloquial register.
findings.replacement: —I thought he might be a gangster, so I couldn’t so much as squeak.

findings.current:
“Didn’t you hear me? Repeat my order, then get it done!”

“…Yes.”

“…We’ll do it.”
findings.defect: The draft turns the second subordinate’s reluctant verbatim repetition into a normal promise, losing the military command-and-response register and the joke built on 실시.
findings.rationale: 복명복창 orders the subordinates to repeat the command back, and the second subordinate specifically echoes 실시 rather than paraphrasing compliance.
findings.replacement:
“Didn’t you hear me? Repeat the order back. Execute!”

“…Yes.”

“…Execute.”

findings.current: “Kids these days. They treat the Team Leader like a piece of shit.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the direct second-person rebuke aimed at the two subordinates into a third-person complaint about unspecified people and adds an absent generational reference.
findings.rationale: 자식들이 addresses the men in front of him, and 팀장 알기를 아주 개똥으로 알아요 directly accuses them of treating their Team Leader like dog shit.
findings.replacement: “You bastards have gotten way too lax. You treat your Team Leader like dog shit.”
findings.source: “자식들이 빠져 가지고 말이야. 팀장 알기를 아주 개똥으로 알아요.”

findings.current: *Whether it’s an ajumma or an ajusshi, people who grow old without growing up are all alike when it comes to pestering young people.*
findings.defect: “Pestering” loses the flirtatious or sexually importunate sense of 치근덕거리다 and weakens Taekyung’s comparison between older men and women hitting on younger people.
findings.rationale: In the immediate context of touching his arm and giving him a sticky look, 치근덕거리다 means making unwanted flirtatious advances, not generic annoyance.
findings.replacement: *Whether it’s an ajumma or an ajusshi, people who grow old without growing up are all alike when it comes to hitting on younger people.*
findings.source: ‘아줌마나 아저씨나, 철없이 나이 먹으면 젊은 애한테 치근덕거리는 건 비슷하다니까.’

findings.current: I greeted Kim Gwondong, who was pretending to recognize me.
findings.defect: The draft adds that Kim Gwondong only pretends to recognize Taekyung; the source says he initiates a familiar acknowledgment or greeting.
findings.rationale: 알은체를 해 오다 means approaching or addressing someone as an acquaintance. It does not state that the recognition itself is feigned.
findings.replacement: I returned Kim Gwondong’s familiar greeting.
findings.source: 나는 알은체를 해 오는 김권동에게 인사를 건넸다.

findings.current: “Young man, what would you like to drink? Coffee? Yulmu tea? Cola?”
findings.defect: The existing yulmu-tea footnote is never referenced, leaving an unused Markdown footnote definition.
findings.rationale: Adding the marker at the term’s occurrence correctly connects the useful cultural explanation already present at the end of the draft.
findings.replacement: “Young man, what would you like to drink? Coffee? Yulmu tea?[^1] Cola?”
findings.source: “젊은 분이 오셨네. 뭐 마실래요? 커피? 율무차? 콜라?”

summary: The draft contains one consequential monetary error, several altered subjects or actions, and localized losses of register, pragmatic meaning, and Markdown consistency.
